I only ever returned things like clothes and computer articles. It depends on the retailer wether you have to pay for your shipping.

My return on Ebay is simply replying it is broken or not arrived yet(which actually happens). And that works well enough.

Last time I returned stuff was when I bought PC parts and something didn't work. I'm not sure what it was, but they basically wanted a 15% restocking fee, which was around $150 for the stuff total. I just had it replaced instead and sold it on ebay.

I have when needed. Had a bulb in my old LED rear projection TV pop. Looked up the purchase on Amazon which said there was a 12 month warranty. They shipped me a new bulb, I shipped the broken one back in the same box and was refunded.

For items that come and I get buyer's remorse, I just resell them online instead of sending them back.

I returned a laptop replacement screen from ebay that didn't fit. I called the customer support from the retailer and they immediately helped me figure out which screen was the right one. It would have taken me a long time to figure that out myself, the naming conventions for the screens were weird. Good, free customer service is a rare thing.

I filled out the return form and sent the wrong screen back to the retailer. I got my 60$ and the right screen a few days later.

I buy a lot of stuff on-line, mostly it's cheaper things (< $50) though so if they don't work out for some reason it's generally no biggie. Recently I took and plunge and bought a tablet from Gearbest out of China. The price was really good ($400 CDN) for essentially a Surface 3 and reviews were generally pretty good so I decided to take the plunge. Turns out the tablet has non-functioning sleep/hibernate modes AND even when the tablet is off the battery completely discharges within 5 days of being unplugged from the wall. Couple that with the 5 hour usable battery life and the tablet is pretty much useless for traveling with, which was the reason I got it in the first place.

Anyhow cue many exchanges with Gearbest customer service in an attempt to get a refund per their "45 days full refund on faulty items" policy. Well it turns out that refund is defined as store credit, which is also stated on the return policy but you have to go looking for it, the sneaky bastards. I acknowledge that I have no excuse for NOT reading the entire returns policy in advance of making the purchase, though I'd received broken items from them before and they had readily sent replacements. Though in those cases the items were < $5 so it's not quite the same, still it did rather set me up to assume the 45 day full refund policy could be taken at face value.

So lesson learned. I now have a rather pricey paperweight that boots both Android 5.1 and Win10 if I'm prepared to leave it plugged into the wall all of the time woopee.

Also they deleted my less than stellar review, and since certified owners can only post 1 review I can't do another. Sneaky bastards.

tl;dr Fuck you Gearbest
